candidate_gaps.title: NoSQL operator injection on login/user-lookup queries (req.body objects passed unvalidated into findOne filters)
candidate_gaps.evidence: app/data/user-dao.js:91-93 (validateLogin: usersCol.findOne({ userName: userName })) and :103-107 (getUserByUserName); reachable because server.js:71 enables bodyParser.json() and app/routes/session.js:54-58 destructures userName/password from req.body with no type check.
candidate_gaps.attack_path: Login accepts a JSON body. An attacker POSTs /login with Content-Type: application/json and body {"userName": {"$gt": ""}} (or {"$regex": "^adm"}). bodyParser.json() turns userName into a query operator object that flows directly into findOne({ userName: <object> }), so the query matches the first/any user document (e.g., the admin, _id:1) instead of an exact-string match. Because handleLoginRequest returns distinct 'Invalid username' (no match) vs 'Invalid password' (match found, password mismatch) responses, the attacker gets a boolean oracle: they can enumerate which users exist and brute-force usernames via $regex without knowing any username up front, and force the auth flow to load the admin document. The only thing preventing a full credential-free bypass is the JS-side strict comparison (fromDB === fromUser) in comparePassword, so this lands as account/user enumeration plus query manipulation rather than direct login bypass — still a pre-auth NoSQL injection.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model's NoSQL finding (TM-002) is scoped only to the $where string-concatenation sink in allocations-dao.js, and TM-016 treats username enumeration purely as a verbose-error-message issue assuming string inputs with rate-limiting as the fix. Neither covers MongoDB query-operator injection ($ne/$gt/$regex) made possible by bodyParser.json() feeding unvalidated object literals into findOne filters across user-dao/profile-dao/benefits-dao — a different sink and a different (pre-auth) attack surface than the authenticated allocations $where path.

confirmed_gaps.title: NoSQL operator injection on login/user-lookup queries (req.body objects passed unvalidated into findOne filters)
confirmed_gaps.evidence: app/data/user-dao.js:91-93 (validateLogin -> usersCol.findOne({ userName: userName })) and :103-107 (getUserByUserName -> findOne({ userName })); server.js:71 (app.use(bodyParser.json())) and app/routes/session.js:54-58 (handleLoginRequest destructures userName/password from req.body with no type check). Strict comparePassword fromDB===fromUser at user-dao.js:60-61 limits this to enumeration/query-manipulation, and distinct error responses (Invalid username vs Invalid password) at session.js:60-98 provide the boolean oracle.
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: findings.json TM-002 scopes NoSQL injection only to the $where string-concatenation sink in allocations-dao.js (authenticated, GET /allocations?threshold=), a different file/sink/injection class. TM-016 treats username enumeration purely as a verbose-error + weak-password + rate-limiting issue assuming string inputs, and TM-004 covers plaintext password comparison as a storage issue. None address MongoDB query-operator injection ($ne/$gt/$regex) made possible by bodyParser.json() feeding unvalidated object literals into the unauthenticated login findOne filter — a distinct pre-auth sink. Likelihood 4 (pre-auth, trivial JSON body) x impact 3-4 (reliable user-enumeration oracle plus forced load of arbitrary/admin user documents) lands >=10.
